title: Thermal design check
summary: Set an illustrative steady tip-temperature limit, solve a cooled fin, and distinguish a conditional pass from the global maximum and uncertain inputs.

steps.title: State the requirement before solving
steps.explain: For this exercise only, require the centre of the insulated tip at [150 mm, 12.5 mm, 1 mm] to remain at or below 40 °C in steady operation. This is an illustrative tip-only requirement, not a product safety limit. The root is held at 120 °C. Define what is limited before looking at a contour.

steps.title: Start the fin Model
steps.explain: Start an empty Model. Its geometry, boundary conditions and numerical material constants match the checked heated-fin-convection example; this guide states their illustrative provenance and adds a design question.

steps.title: Use Celsius for the result
steps.explain: The engine stores absolute temperature in kelvin. Celsius here is a display unit; 20 degC is not 20 K.

steps.title: Add the thin aluminium fin
steps.explain: The fin is 150 mm long, 25 mm wide and 2 mm thick. The held root is x = 0; the tip to check is x = 150 mm.

steps.title: Record conductivity
steps.explain: Use the assumed illustrative aluminium conductivity k = 205 W/(m K). These reference constants are not certified 6061-T6 or EN 573-3 material data. Density and heat capacity are recorded for completeness but do not turn a heat-steady Step into a transient simulation.

doIt.name: aluminium
doIt.source: Assumed illustrative aluminium constants for the analytical fin reference; not a certified material grade

steps.title: Assign aluminium to the fin
steps.explain: A Material applies only after it is assigned to the Body.

steps.title: Use the checked quadratic mesh
steps.explain: Use the existing example mesh: 30 × 5 × 2 cells with quadratic interpolation. Compare a probe with an independent formula as well as inspecting the contour.

steps.title: Hold the root at 120 °C
steps.explain: The heat source maintains a fixed root temperature, deliberately above the tip requirement. An all-body temperature limit of 40 °C would already fail.

steps.title: Cool the upper face
steps.explain: Air at 20 °C removes heat with the assumed h = 50 W/(m² K). This boundary coefficient is supplied; there is no fluid-flow calculation.

steps.title: Cool the lower face
steps.explain: Apply the same ambient and coefficient to the lower long face.

steps.title: Cool the front edge
steps.explain: Include the thin front long face. The analytical perimeter includes all four long faces.

steps.title: Cool the back edge
steps.explain: Complete the cooled perimeter. Leave the tip without a heat boundary Command: it is insulated, matching the adiabatic-tip reference.

steps.title: Add the steady thermal Step
steps.explain: Include the held root and four convection loads. heat-steady predicts equilibrium after transients decay; it gives no warm-up time or transient peak.

steps.title: Solve the stated assumptions
steps.explain: Run the Step. Expect about 37.41 °C at the tip, compared with 37.39 °C from the independent one-dimensional fin solution. Read the actual result before deciding.

steps.title: Probe the tip, not the global maximum
steps.explain: Choose Do it for me to fit the solved fin in the viewer; this changes only the camera. Read the centre of the tip. In a script or browser console, run `await fem.query.probe({field: "temperature", at: ["150 mm", "12.5 mm", "1 mm"]})`. With Celsius selected, confirm value.unit is degC and read value.value: expect about 37.41 °C. The root/global maximum is about 120 °C and answers a different question. Choose Next after inspecting the result.

steps.title: Make the bounded decision
steps.explain: For this tip-only requirement, 37.41 °C ≤ 40 °C: pass under the assumed steady conditions, with about 2.59 K of margin. Celsius differences and kelvin differences have the same size. A 40 °C limit anywhere in the Body would fail at the 120 °C root. Neither decision describes a transient.

steps.title: Check what could change the decision
steps.explain: The margin depends on convection, ambient and root temperatures, conductivity and geometry. The same analytical fin formula at h = 25 W/(m² K) predicts about 54.65 °C at the tip: a fail. That is an analytical sensitivity estimate, not a second FEM solve performed here. To solve it, edit all four convection loads consistently and solve conduct again. A small mesh error does not bound uncertain inputs.

steps.title: The independent reference and equivalent terminology
steps.explain: The reference assumes a nearly uniform cross-section temperature, four convecting long faces and an insulated tip. Compare the value before accepting the design decision.
steps.theory:
The adiabatic-tip fin solution is
$$T(x)=T_\infty+(T_b-T_\infty)\frac{\cosh m(L-x)}{\cosh mL},\qquad m=\sqrt{\frac{hP}{kA}}.$$
Here $L=0.15\,\mathrm m$, $A=0.025\times0.002=5\times10^{-5}\,\mathrm{m^2}$, $P=2(0.025+0.002)=0.054\,\mathrm m$ and $k=205\,\mathrm{W/(m\,K)}$. With $h=50\,\mathrm{W/(m^2\,K)}$, $T_b=120\,^\circ\mathrm C$ and $T_\infty=20\,^\circ\mathrm C$, the independent reference gives $T(L)=37.3946\,^\circ\mathrm C$ versus about $37.41\,^\circ\mathrm C$ computed. The through-thickness Biot number $h(t/2)/k=2.44\times10^{-4}$ supports the uniform cross-section approximation; it does not remove uncertainty in $h$.

**Decision:** the illustrative requirement is $T_{tip}\le40\,^\circ\mathrm C$, with margin $40-T_{tip}\approx2.59\,\mathrm K$. It passes only this steady tip-temperature check. The global maximum is the prescribed $120\,^\circ\mathrm C$ root. There is no transient peak calculation, fluid solver or automatic design certification.

**Equivalent terminology.** `heat-steady` corresponds to an Abaqus steady-state heat-transfer step, Ansys Steady-State Thermal, or a Nastran steady-state heat-transfer solution. `constraint.temperature` is a prescribed temperature boundary; `load.convection` is a film/convection boundary. A temperature probe or requested nodal temperature supplies the value compared with a requirement. Names vary by product and do not imply identical elements or solvers.

This is re-authored around FEM Lab's existing fin example and its analytical reference. Autodesk Fusion's Thermal analysis tutorial is a reference for the design-question learning goal: https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/ENU/Fusion-Simulate/files/GUID-4B1F8D61-6F33-4E6A-B08A-4E562026762C.htm .
